title: Boss: the full process
summary: Plan, trace, test and debug your way through four problems, then ship Delve: wire the whole game together from memory.

steps.title: Final boss
body: Everything from this topic at once. For each problem: restate it, work two examples by hand (one an edge case), write pseudocode, then code. The tests include edge cases, so think about empty and single inputs before you run.

steps.title: Run-length encoding
prompt: Write `string Encode(string s)` that compresses runs of the same character as the character followed by its count.
`Encode("aaabcc")` is `"a3b1c2"`. `Encode("")` is `""`.
hints: Outer loop: start a new run at position `i`. Inner loop: advance `i` while the character matches.
The `i < s.Length` check must come **first** in the inner condition: short-circuiting guards the index.

steps.title: Balanced brackets
prompt: Write `bool Balanced(string s)` for strings made of `(` and `)`. They are balanced when every `(` has a matching `)` after it.
Plan: keep a `depth` counter. `(` adds one, `)` subtracts one. If depth ever goes **below zero**, a `)` came too early. At the end, depth must be exactly zero.
`"(())()"` is balanced; `")("` and `"(()"` are not.
hints: The invariant: `depth` is the number of currently open brackets.
Check `depth < 0` inside the loop, and `depth == 0` after it.

steps.title: Binary search
prompt: Write `int Find(int[] sorted, int target)` returning the index of `target` in a **sorted** array, or `-1` if it is absent. Do not scan every item: keep a range `lo..hi`, look at the middle, and throw away the half that cannot contain the target.
Edge cases to work by hand first: empty array, one item, target smaller than everything, target larger than everything.

forbid.message: Narrows a range instead of scanning

hints: Loop `while (lo <= hi)`. With `<` you would never check a range of one item.
If the middle is too small, the target is to the right: `lo = mid + 1`. Otherwise `hi = mid - 1`.

steps.title: The spiral map
prompt: When you pick up a floor's key in Delve, the map unrolls in a **spiral** from the top-left corner: the engine numbers every cell, asks your `Spiral` for the order, and reveals the first half.
Write `List<int> Spiral(int[,] g)` returning the values of a rectangular grid read clockwise in a spiral from the top-left. `g.GetLength(0)` is the number of rows, `g.GetLength(1)` the columns.
```text

Break it down: keep four boundaries (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`). Read the top row, then the right column, then the bottom row backwards, then the left column upwards, shrinking a boundary after each. Watch the single-row and single-column edge cases.
Keep the `static` in front: this is a Delve piece.
solution: for (int c = left; c <= right; c++) result.Add(g[top, c]);
for (int r = top; r <= bottom; r++) result.Add(g[r, right]);
for (int c = right; c >= left; c--) result.Add(g[bottom, c]);
for (int r = bottom; r >= top; r--) result.Add(g[r, left]);
hints: After reading the top row, `top++`. After the right column, `right--`. Then bottom row and left column.
Before reading the bottom row, check `top <= bottom` again; before the left column, check `left <= right`. Otherwise a single row or column is read twice.

forbid.message: Every function starts with `static` (Delve keeps its pieces in one static class)

build.title: Spiral map reveal
build.unlocks: Picking up a key in Delve unrolls the map in a spiral.

steps.title: Ship Delve
prompt: **The last piece.** Every part of Delve exists and every one of them is yours. Until now the game has been playing floor 1 only; this function wires the whole run together. It is a **cold** step: an empty editor, no hints. You know every part.
Write **`static string Play()`**, using the engine's functions and constants:
| Name | What it does |
| `Banner()` | your title screen |
| `NewGame()` | asks for a save code; returns the floor to start on (1 for a new game) |
| `StartFloor(floor)` | carves the floor and shows it |
| `GameLoop(TurnsPerFloor)` | your game loop; returns `"descend"`, `"dead"`, `"quit"` or `"torch out"` |
| `Victory()` | the escape, with your ClimbStory |
| `GameOver(result, floor)` | the score, the save code and your high score board |
| `MaxFloors`, `TurnsPerFloor` | constants |

The run: show the banner, start on the floor `NewGame()` gives, and play floor after floor up to `MaxFloors`. When a floor's loop ends with anything but `"descend"`, call `GameOver(result, floor)` for that floor and return the result. After the last floor is cleared, call `Victory()`, then `GameOver("won", MaxFloors)`, and return `"won"`.
The checks give `Play` a stand-in engine with 3 floors and scripted floor results, and compare what happens, call by call.

static string GameLoop(int maxTurns) { Console.WriteLine($"loop {maxTurns}"); return DojoEngine.Results.Dequeue(); }
static void GameOver(string result, int floor) => Console.WriteLine($"over {result} {floor}");
static class DojoEngine { public static int Start = 1; public static Queue<string> Results = new(); }

steps.explain: That is Delve, finished: open **Builds**, open it as a Code space and run `dotnet run`. Every line that decides what happens in that game is one you wrote.
